cards.explanation: The answer is Jerusalem. Verse 13 says John left them at Perga to return there. The text doesn't tell us why he went, so I'm not guessing out loud. I'll just say that when a teammate heads back mid-journey, the rest of the crew still has dough to roll.

The answer is False. The leaders don't say a word about staying quiet. They send word in verse 15: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.” Two visitors just sat down, and they got handed the floor.

The answer is a word of encouragement. The leaders say, “…if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.” They send word to the two visitors after the reading from the Law and the Prophets. Notice they ask politely, and Paul takes them up on it. Wait until you see how much encouragement fits in one sermon.

The answer is men of Israel and Gentiles who fear God. Paul says, “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!” (Acts 13:16). So he addresses two groups in one room, and he speaks to both at once. Nobody in that synagogue gets left out of the invitation to listen, friends.
The answer is True. Paul says in verse 18, “He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.” Forty years, friends. Say it out loud and it sounds even longer.

The answer is judges. Verse 20 says, “After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.” Paul runs through a lot of history fast, and judges are one stop on the way. Keep that word handy, because the king comes right after.

The answer is David son of Jesse. Paul says God testified about him: “I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.” (Acts 13:22). That's God's own testimony about a king. I'd frame that on my bakery wall if somebody said it about me.

The answer is David the king. Paul says in verse 23, “From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.” The man right before that verse is David. So the Savior comes from David's line, and Paul says it plainly.

The answer is False. In Acts 13:25 John says, “Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One.” He says the One coming after him is someone whose sandals he isn't worthy to untie. That's John making it clear he isn't the main event.

The answer is Pilate. Verse 28 says that though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed. It's a heavy line, and I think it hurts a little to read. Paul says it plainly, so I will too.

The answer is True. Verse 31 says that for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Paul adds, “They are now His witnesses to our people.” These aren't strangers passing along a rumor, friends. They're the ones who traveled with Him.

The answer is that David's body was buried and saw decay. Verse 36 says David “…fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.” Paul sets that next to Jesus, who did not see decay (Acts 13:37). David served God's purpose in his own generation, and Paul tells us how his story ended, plain as flour.

The answer is believes. Paul says, “Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.” (Acts 13:39). Notice the word everyone. That's a wide door, friends, and Paul throws it open.

The answer is that they'd never believe it if told. Verse 41 says, “For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.” That's the warning to scoffers, and Paul ends the sermon on it. It's a serious closing, so I'll leave it serious.

The answer is to continue the message next Sabbath. Verse 42 says the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath. They don't wait for the door to hit them on the way out, friends. They want more.

The answer is grace. Verse 43 says Paul and Barnabas spoke to the many Jews and devout converts who followed them, and urged them to continue in the grace of God. Just before that, in verse 39, Paul said that through Jesus everyone who believes is justified. Grace is a good word to carry out of a synagogue, and I'd stitch it on my apron if I had the room.

The answer is jealousy. Verse 44 says nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord. Then verse 45 says when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. I think that's a hard moment to read.
The answer is False. Acts 13:46 says Paul and Barnabas “…answered them boldly…” They don't back down. They go on to say, “…we now turn to the Gentiles.”

The answer is the Gentiles. Verse 46 says, “…we now turn to the Gentiles.” Paul and Barnabas say it was necessary to speak God's word to the Jews first, and then they make the turn. That's the direction of the whole next part.

The answer is a light for the Gentiles. Verse 47 has the Lord's words: “I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.” Paul and Barnabas say this is what the Lord commanded them. That's a big job, and it comes from Him.

The answer is True. Verse 48 says, “…all who were appointed for eternal life believed.” That's after the Gentiles heard the news and rejoiced. The text states it plainly, and I'll keep it exactly there.

The answer is throughout that region. Verse 49 says, “And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.” Verse 44 already says nearly the whole city gathered to hear it. The word covers a whole region, and it didn't need a group chat to do it.

The answer is that it drives them out of the district. Verse 50 says the Jews incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district. It's a heavy moment, and I think it stings a little.

The answers are dust and Iconium. Verse 51 says they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium. It's a clear move, no words needed. I spent years in a junk drawer under a pile of dust, friends, and I never made a point that good with it. The journey doesn't stop when they're driven out of a district.

The answer is True. Verse 52 says, “And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.” That's right after Paul and Barnabas get driven out. The text puts the joy and the Holy Spirit together, and I'll leave it just as it is.
